_README: question forms for the question_form axis
uses timeqa's slots, so this file and the relations.json templates share one renderer (question_form.py):
$1  subject           - entity link as text, e.g. 'Ian Gibson (politician)'
$4  range expression  - e.g. 'from May 1997 to May 2001' (mode 'accumulate')
$m  relation meaning  - e.g. 'position held'    (added, not in timeqa)
relation_mode picks the variant of an authored form, like timeqa's templates. 'n/a' uses accumulate
dataset_verbatim - timeqa's question as is, the control
dataset_template - the relation's own template at template_index. 174 of 2674 scored dev rows
have one template, so index > 0 doesn't apply to all rows (hence applied/applicable)
authored         - our own forms, apply to every row as $m covers all 52 relation codes in dev

timeqa_source.description: timeqa's question text as is, the control

timeqa_alt.description: the relation's first own template that doesn't match timeqa's question, a real timeqa alternative. a fixed index would leave ~35% of rows the same as the control, as timeqa picked templates per question

declarative.description: no question framing, just subject, relation, time

keyword.description: search style, content words only, no function words or punctuation

time_first.description: same tokens as declarative with the time moved to the front, only the date position changes

no_relation.description: no relation, tests how much retrieval relies on the relation phrase
